checks.label: Managed Device State (Device/Profile Owner)
checks.command: D=$(dumpsys device_policy 2>/dev/null); DO=$(printf '%s' "$D" | grep -iA1 'Device Owner' | grep -iE 'ComponentInfo|admin='); PO=$(printf '%s' "$D" | grep -iA1 'Profile Owner' | grep -iE 'ComponentInfo|admin='); if [ -n "$DO" ]; then echo MANAGED_DEVICE_OWNER; elif [ -n "$PO" ]; then echo MANAGED_PROFILE_OWNER; else echo UNMANAGED; fi
checks.description: Reports whether the device is under enterprise management: a Device Owner (fully managed), a Profile Owner (work profile), or UNMANAGED. The DevicePolicyManager policies below only apply on managed devices; on an UNMANAGED device they are absent and reported empty, which is expected, not a finding.
checks.remediation: Informational. For POS/kiosk/medical fleets the device should be a Device Owner managed device. If UNMANAGED unexpectedly, the management profile may have been removed.

checks.label: Keyguard Disabled Features (Policy)
checks.description: Surfaces DevicePolicyManager.getKeyguardDisabledFeatures state - which lockscreen features an admin disabled (secure camera, secure notifications, trust agents, biometrics, widgets). Evidence collector for managed devices; empty on unmanaged devices. Field names vary by Android version so this matches several variants.
checks.remediation: On a kiosk/POS device, review which keyguard features the DPC disabled. Disabling secure-camera and unredacted-notifications on the lock screen reduces data exposure.

checks.label: Camera Disabled By Policy
checks.description: Surfaces DevicePolicyManager.getCameraDisabled policy state (distinct from the /dev/video* device-node check in USB_SECURITY). On managed POS/kiosk devices the camera is often disabled by policy. Empty on unmanaged devices.
checks.remediation: If the device should not use the camera (payment terminal, kiosk), confirm the DPC has set setCameraDisabled(true).

checks.label: Lock & Wipe Policy (Max Time To Lock / Failed-Password Wipe)
checks.description: Surfaces DevicePolicyManager getMaximumTimeToLock and getMaximumFailedPasswordsForWipe. A short max-time-to-lock and a failed-password wipe threshold are key anti-theft controls for fleet devices. Evidence collector; empty on unmanaged devices.
checks.remediation: For lost/stolen device resilience, set a short maximum time to lock and a sane failed-password wipe threshold via the DPC.

checks.label: Password Policy (Complexity / Expiration / History / Strong-Auth)
checks.command: dumpsys device_policy 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'password complexity|passwordcomplexity|requiredpasswordcomplexity|password expiration|expiredate|password history|history length|strong auth|strongauthunlocktimeout|requiredstrongauth|password quality|passwordquality' | head -10
checks.description: Surfaces the admin-imposed screen-lock password policy: required complexity, expiration timeout, history length and required strong-auth timeout. Evidence collector for managed devices; empty on unmanaged. Note: getPasswordComplexity itself is preferred over the deprecated password-quality getters.
checks.remediation: Review the password policy against your deployment standard (e.g. PASSWORD_COMPLEXITY_HIGH for devices handling card or patient data).

checks.label: Audit Logging (Security / Network Logging)
checks.description: Surfaces DevicePolicyManager isSecurityLoggingEnabled and isNetworkLoggingEnabled. Security and network logging are central forensic controls for managed fleets. Evidence collector; empty on unmanaged devices.
checks.remediation: For regulated deployments, enable security logging (and network logging where permitted) via the DPC so incidents are auditable.

checks.label: USB Data Signaling Policy
checks.command: dumpsys device_policy 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'usb data signaling|usbdatasignaling|usb signaling|musbdatasignaling' | head -4
checks.description: Surfaces DevicePolicyManager isUsbDataSignalingEnabled policy state. Disabling USB data signaling (charging only) hardens POS and kiosk devices against juice-jacking and USB-based attacks. Evidence collector; empty on unmanaged or unsupported devices.
checks.remediation: On dedicated-function devices, disable USB data signaling via the DPC (setUsbDataSignalingEnabled(false)) where the hardware supports it.

checks.label: Common Criteria Mode
checks.description: Surfaces DevicePolicyManager isCommonCriteriaModeEnabled. Common Criteria mode tightens Bluetooth long-term-key and Wi-Fi config integrity protection (AES-GCM) to meet CC certification. Evidence collector; empty on unmanaged devices.
checks.remediation: For deployments requiring Common Criteria assurance, enable it via setCommonCriteriaModeEnabled(true). Note enabling it can drop existing Wi-Fi configurations.

checks.label: Runtime Memory Tagging (MTE) Mode
checks.command: M=$(getprop arm64.memtag.bootctl 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$M" ] && M=$(getprop persist.arm64.memtag.default 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$M" ] && echo "$M" || echo NONE
checks.description: Reports the runtime MTE (Memory Tagging Extension) boot control mode via getprop, complementing the kernel-config check (CONFIG_ARM64_MTE) in SYSTEM. 'memtag' / 'memtag-once' means MTE is active at runtime; NONE means off. DevicePolicyManager.getMtePolicy can enforce this on managed devices. MTE off is common for performance reasons, so this is informational posture.
checks.remediation: For high-value targets, enable MTE via the DPC (setMtePolicy(MTE_ENABLED)) on ARMv8.5+ hardware. Reboot required for changes to take effect.

checks.label: App Control Policy (User-Control-Disabled / Personal Apps Suspended)
checks.command: dumpsys device_policy 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'user control disabled|usercontroldisabled|protectedpackages|personal apps suspended|personalappssuspended|suspendpersonalapps' | head -6
checks.description: Surfaces getUserControlDisabledPackages (apps the user cannot force-stop or clear) and getPersonalAppsSuspendedReasons. Evidence collector for managed devices; empty on unmanaged. On a kiosk, the operator app is typically user-control-disabled so it cannot be killed.
checks.remediation: On dedicated devices, confirm the operator/kiosk app is in the user-control-disabled list so users cannot force-stop it.

checks.label: Runtime Permission Grant Policy
checks.description: Surfaces DevicePolicyManager.getPermissionPolicy - whether the admin auto-grants, auto-denies, or prompts for runtime permission requests. Auto-grant on a managed device is worth reviewing because it removes the user from sensitive-permission decisions. Evidence collector; empty on unmanaged devices.
checks.remediation: Review the permission grant policy. Auto-granting sensor permissions (location, camera, mic) device-wide should be justified by the deployment.

checks.label: Admin Wi-Fi Configuration Lockdown
checks.command: L=$(settings get global wifi_device_owner_configs_lockdown 2>/dev/null); P=$(dumpsys device_policy 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'wifi ssid policy|wifissidpolicy|ssidallowlist|ssiddenylist|minimum.*wifi.*security|minimumrequiredwifisecurity' | head -4); echo "lockdown=$L"; [ -n "$P" ] && printf '%s\n' "$P"
checks.description: Surfaces hasLockdownAdminConfiguredNetworks (global wifi_device_owner_configs_lockdown) plus any Wi-Fi SSID allow/deny policy and minimum Wi-Fi security level set by the admin. lockdown=1 means the user cannot modify admin-configured networks. Evidence collector.
checks.remediation: On managed fleets, lock down admin-configured Wi-Fi (setConfiguredNetworksLockdownState(true)) and set a minimum Wi-Fi security level so devices cannot join open networks.

checks.label: A15 Privacy Policies (Content Protection / Nearby Streaming)
checks.description: Surfaces Android 15 era DevicePolicyManager privacy policies: getContentProtectionPolicy (scanning for deceptive apps) and the nearby app/notification streaming policies. Evidence collector for managed devices; empty on unmanaged or pre-A15.
checks.remediation: Review content protection and nearby-streaming policies for deployments where screen/notification content is sensitive.

checks.label: System Update Policy
checks.description: Surfaces DevicePolicyManager.getSystemUpdatePolicy - whether the admin defers, windows, or auto-installs OTA updates, and any configured freeze periods. Evidence collector for managed devices. Complements the SPL-currency check in SYSTEM/CVE_INDICATORS.
checks.remediation: Confirm the system update policy keeps devices patched. Long freeze periods or indefinite deferral conflict with a current security patch level.

checks.label: Permitted Accessibility / Input Methods (Admin Allowlist)
checks.description: Surfaces the DPM admin allowlists getPermittedAccessibilityServices and getPermittedInputMethods. These are distinct from the INPUT category checks, which read the settings.secure enabled lists - here we show the admin-enforced allowlist. An empty allowlist (when set) means only system services are permitted, which is the locked-down state.
checks.remediation: On locked-down devices, restrict accessibility services and input methods to an explicit allowlist (or system-only) via the DPC to block keyloggers and screen scrapers.
